SorobanAuthorizedInvocation tree (rootInvocation, subInvocations<>) (stage H): Each node matched at most once against actual calls.
SorobanAuthorizedInvocation tree (rootInvocation, subInvocations<>) (stage H): No depth limiter of its own; bounded only by the XDR decode depth of 500 and transaction size.

ContractEvent.contractID, topics and data, for events of type CONTRACT: The host sets contractID to the contract that is executing; a contract cannot choose it. Topics and data are whatever that contract passes.
ContractEvent.contractID, topics and data, for events of type CONTRACT (stage H): The contract_event host function takes only topics and data; the host fills contract_id from the current frame.

ContractEvent.contractID, topics and data, for events of type CONTRACT (stage A): The contract ID of an asset's Stellar Asset Contract is a function of the network ID and the asset (getAssetContractID); core uses it for the events it emits itself.
A reader may assume that the event was emitted by the contract named in contractID.

A reader must not assume that a transfer-shaped event moved the asset or touched the accounts it names. Key every movement on the emitting contract ID. Treat an event as a movement of a classic asset only when contractID equals the Stellar Asset Contract ID derived from that asset and the network ID. Never add a participant because an arbitrary contract's event names it.
stellar-core validates some transaction fields and passes others through untouched.
A field that core passes through is whatever the submitter put there, so read it as attacker-controlled input.
Work out who a transaction affected from ledger meta, not from the envelope.
The envelope records what the submitter claimed; meta records what core changed.

A transaction that appears in a ledger passed every stateless check against the last closed ledger, because every validator re-runs those checks on every transaction in a proposed transaction set (source).
A transaction that appears with a failed result may have failed any stateful check at apply time, and it is still in the ledger and still paid a fee (source).
Branch on `TransactionResult.result.code`, never on the envelope alone.
D0 XDR decode | Shape, lengths, padding and union discriminants; no meaning. The decoder's stack limit is 1500 units | main.cpp L425
D1 protocol XDR check | Envelope nesting depth and which XDR arms the current protocol allows | TransactionUtils.cpp L1350-1378
D2 fee XDR check | A Soroban transaction has a v1 envelope with Soroban data; resource fee between 0 and 2^50 stroops | TransactionFrame.cpp L1774-1790
C1 stateless checks | Envelope type, preconditions, Soroban resources, time and ledger bounds, minimum fee, source account exists | TransactionFrame.cpp L1241-1495
C2 account checks | Sequence number, minimum sequence age and gap, transaction signatures, balance covers the fee | TransactionFrame.cpp L1608-1728
C3 operation checks | Operation source, operation threshold, operation-specific shape checks | OperationFrame.cpp L283-363
C4 signatures used | Every signature was used by some signer | SignatureChecker.cpp L172-191
T transaction set | Every validator re-runs C1 to C4 for every transaction against the last closed ledger | TxSetFrame.cpp L1789-1845
A apply | C1 to C4 again against the ledger as it stands at that point, then the operations | TransactionFrame.cpp L2028-2098
H Soroban host | Host function and authorization decoding, value conversion, authorization, execution | e2e_invoke.rs L470-578
A closed ledger is final: a transaction that is in a ledger stays there with the result it got.

Each line names the validation stage, the code that performs the check, what you may assume, what you must not assume, the result code core returns when the check fails, and the corpus entries that demonstrate it.

The envelope records what the submitter claimed; ledger meta records what core changed.

The authoritative sources of who a transaction affected are the fee-processing changes, the transaction-level changes before and after, each operation's ledger-entry changes, the Soroban ledger changes and consensus contract events.
Events for classic operations and fees are a convenience view that exists only on nodes with the flag set.

sentence: Operation sources and destinations in its envelope are claimed, not affected.
This includes counterparties the envelope never names, such as the sellers of crossed offers and liquidity pools (`cap-0038/claim-atoms-pool-and-order-book-mixed`).
An event is evidence of what its emitting contract says, nothing more: the host sets the contract ID, the contract chooses topics and data, and anyone can deploy a contract.

Record a token movement under the emitting contract ID, and treat it as a movement of a classic asset only when that ID equals the Stellar Asset Contract ID derived from the asset and the network ID; the asset named in the fourth topic does not prove it.
Do not add an account to the participant set because an event names it: an account is a participant when ledger-entry changes show it was touched.
If the product needs "addresses named in events of contract C", store that as its own relation, attributed to C.
